validity.recommendation: none — existence and classification robustly confirmed by non-GEM, non-wiki sources
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and well documented outside gem.wiki. (1) An archived Ukrainian news report (kp.ua, dated 2009-01-05) describes Russia halting gas supply on the 'Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka' pipeline, causing a 1.1 million m3/hour shortfall to Kharkiv Oblast — independent, dated, contemporaneous confirmation the line was a real, gas-carrying import route from Russia into Kharkiv Oblast. (2) Both en.wikipedia's 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' and ru.wikipedia's 'Gazotransportnaya sistema Ukrainy' articles independently name the Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka pipeline and its Valuyki (Belgorod Oblast) entry metering station into Ukraine, matching the sheet's Russia->Ukraine routing. (3) Most decisively: this exact pipeline is the subject of extensive, ongoing 2025-2026 war reporting — Kyiv Independent, United24 Media, and Meduza (three separately-owned, editorially independent outlets) all describe Russian troops using an abandoned gas pipeline crossing the Oskil River near Kupiansk to infiltrate Ukrainian lines; Kyiv Independent names it specifically as 'the Shebelinka-Ostrogozhsk gas pipeline, originally built during the Soviet era to transport gas from Kharkiv Oblast to Russia' and gives its diameter as 1-1.2 m (consistent with the sheet's 40in/~1.02m). This independently confirms the pipe physically exists, is buried, runs Kharkiv Oblast<->Russia across the Oskil river corridor, and currently carries no gas (used empty as an infiltration tunnel) — fully consistent with a non-operating ('mothballed') classification. CLASSIFICATION: transmission trunk (not gathering/feeder) is correct — every source describes it as a main interstate/interregional gas transmission line. One nuance for the record, not a defect: the pipeline's ORIGINAL Soviet-era purpose (per ngpedia.ru's Shebelinka field history, citing 1950s-1970s construction) was apparently to export Shebelinka field gas TO the Russian/central system, i.e. flow Ukraine->Russia — the opposite direction implied by the sheet's Start=Ostrogozhsk(Russia)/End=Shebelinka(Ukraine). By the 1980s-2000s (as Shebelinka's own field output declined) the documented use was import Russia->Ukraine (matches the 2009 disruption report and gem.wiki's framing). GEM's Start/End fields are a geographic listing, not a flow-direction assertion, so this is not treated as an error, just worth noting if the pipeline is ever split/re-dated.

validity.recommendation: verify Owner2's exact legal entity (TSOU vs its asset-holding subsidiary MGU) before next update; keep the Gazprom/Ukraine-state split
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1=Gazprom PJSC / Owner2=Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine (TSOU) is the correct MODEL for a genuinely cross-border line per the country guidance's Gazprom-never-owns-Ukrainian-soil rule read together with its cross-border exception: Gazprom for the Russian section (Ostrogozhsk side), the Ukrainian state entity for the Ukrainian section (Shebelinka side) — this is not the 'Gazprom owns 100% of a wholly-Ukrainian row' error pattern the guidance warns about, since this pipeline genuinely crosses the border. One unresolved precision point: gem.wiki's own (uncitable) text says 'In 2020, Ukrainian operations transferred to state-owned JSC Mahistralni Hazoprovody Ukrainy [MGU]' — MGU is the asset-holding subsidiary within the TSOU group, distinct from TSOU itself (TSOU is the licensed system operator; MGU reportedly holds/leases specific pipeline assets to it, mirroring the Ukrtransgaz->TSOU/MGU unbundling described in the country's standing guidance). I could not independently (non-gem.wiki) confirm whether 'TSOU' or 'MGU' is the more precise legal owner-of-record for this specific pipeline, so I am not proposing a change, only flagging it for the next researcher who works ownership refs on this row.

validity.recommendation: leave Length/Capacity/StartYear1 refs UNRESOLVED — no independent source with the exact figures found; do not fabricate
validity.researcher_notes: Could not independently corroborate the sheet's exact numeric values beyond gem.wiki's own (uncitable, per-citation-unclear) figures: Length=312km, Capacity=22.50 bcm/y (gem.wiki text itself says '23 billion cubic meters annually', a ~2% rounding difference, not a real conflict), Diameter=40in. All open-web and Russian/Ukrainian-language searches (ngpedia.ru Shebelinka field history, ru.wikipedia gas-field and GTS articles, spravochnick.ru) confirm the pipeline's EXISTENCE and general route but give no length/diameter/capacity numbers for this specific line. The closest independent corroboration is qualitative: Kyiv Independent's war reporting describes soldiers crawling through '1-1.2 meter diameter pipes' near Kupiansk, which brackets but does not precisely confirm 40in (~1.02m) — treated as supportive context, not a value-matching reference, so not staged as a Diameter ref. StartYear1=1981 is the one figure with a potential (not confirmed) conflict: ngpedia.ru's Shebelinka-field history states the original Shebelinka-Ostrogozhsk trunk was built as part of 1950s-1970s Soviet development of the field (exporting Shebelinka gas toward the central/Russian system), which is materially earlier than 1981. It is plausible 1981 refers to a later expansion/second thread (e.g. for the subsequent Russia->Ukraine import use) rather than the original build, but I could not resolve which; flagging rather than silently keeping or changing 1981.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent-language Wikipedia articles on Ukraine's gas transmission system both name the Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka line as part of the natural GAS transmission network entering via Valuyki; uncontested fact.

Described consistently as a main interstate transmission trunk (not a gathering/feeder line) both in the GTS-system Wikipedia article and in the Kyiv Independent's description of it as a large interregional trunk line, correct classification.

en.wikipedia's GTS-of-Ukraine article names the Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka pipeline's Valuyki entry point from Russia (Belgorod Oblast, adjacent to Voronezh Oblast where Ostrogozhsk sits); Kyiv Independent independently confirms the line crosses the Oskil River near Kupiansk in Kharkiv Oblast, i.e. running toward Shebelinka. Together these corroborate the Russia(Voronezh)->Ukraine(Kharkiv/Shebelinka) routing. Tier medium rather than high because the two Wikipedia-language editions are not counted as a second fully independent leg on their own.

Three separately-owned outlets (Kyiv Independent, United24 Media, Meduza), reporting through Feb 2026, all describe this pipeline as empty of gas and abandoned, now used as a war infiltration tunnel and progressively holed/flooded by Ukrainian forces — none report any gas flow. This directly supports 'not operating'; see the linked status_reviews entry for the confirm-vs-retired discussion.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched Russian/Ukrainian/English sources for anything newer than the sheet's 2023-09-11 LastUpdated. Found extensive, dated 2025-2026 war reporting (Meduza 2025-09-15; Kyiv Independent, multiple pieces through ~2026-02; United24 Media, published 2026-01-20/updated 2026-02-02) that this exact pipeline — empty of gas, abandoned since well before the war per Gazprom's own 2020 liquidation of the Valuyki CS-2 compressor station — is now being used by Russian troops as an infiltration tunnel near Kupiansk, and is progressively being holed by Ukrainian air strikes and deliberately flooded to disable the infiltration route. No source describes any gas flow or plan to restore one; Russia-Ukraine transit ended entirely 2025-01-01 per the country's standing context, further reinforcing there is no live use case for this Russia->Ukraine import line. 'Mothballed' (idle, not formally decommissioned) remains a defensible read since I found no formal retirement declaration by either Gazprom or the Ukrainian side — but the case for upgrading to 'retired' is real and building: the compressor station was already being liquidated pre-war (2020), the whole transit relationship it once served ended 2025-01-01, and the pipe itself is now being deliberately destroyed/flooded as war damage. Flagging this combination for the Update leg to weigh a Status change to 'retired' rather than proposing it here without a direct decommissioning declaration.

summary: P0788 (Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka): existence and classification strongly reconfirmed via non-wiki sources, most notably 2025-2026 war reporting (Kyiv Independent/United24/Meduza) on the pipe's use as a Kupiansk infiltration tunnel, which also supports current Status=mothballed (verdict=confirm) though a case for upgrading to retired is flagged for Update; refs added for Fuel/PipelineType/Location/Status; Length, Capacity, Diameter, StartYear1 (1981 vs. a possible 1950s-70s original-build conflict) and Owner (TSOU vs MGU precision) left UNRESOLVED — no fabricated refs; no duplicate found against the roster.
